== Biography ==
{{African-American Sticker}}

Lloyd was born in 1836. He is the son of [[Glasgow-3823|Samuel Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-3824|Elizabeth Glasgow]].


== Research Notes ==
=== Father review, 12 November 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-3823|Samuel Glasgow]] is now assessed at 93% (strongly supported), previously 86% probable. The published transcription of Henrietta Enos's 11 November 1916 obituary calls Samuel Glasco her father and Lloyd her brother. The distinctive Oxford brickyard/Liberia family matches the held 1850 Samuel/Elizabeth household containing Henrietta and Lloyd. The common paternal surname, explicit sibling statement and coherent family support inferring Samuel as Lloyd's father; no concrete alternative parentage is known. The father need not remain merely probable because the article states the relationship through his sister.

The newspaper is known through a 2018 published transcription, not an inspected original issue. Its 1826 birth statement conflicts with its age eighty in 1916 and the held 1850 age; its 1849 migration also conflicts with the university account of 1859. Those dates are not adopted or silently corrected. The explicit father and sibling clauses, distinctive occupation/migration and known family sequence support the identification despite those narrative errors. Mother Elizabeth and Samuel’s unknown father remain separate; no new father is attached.

Source: [https://blackintoledo.wordpress.com/2018/07/27/granville-lee-enos-civil-war-soldier-and-connection-to-glasgow-glasco-and-davis-families-of-chester-county-pa/ Daily Local News, 11 November 1916 obituary, published transcription]. The older review below is retained as assessment history; this review supersedes its father percentage.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-3823]] is assessed at 86% (probable). Lloyd's 1836 birth and 1850 entry in Samuel and Elizabeth's family fit the established sibling sequence and Samuel's age. This is a strong household inference with no relationship column or later parent statement held.

Selected Glasgow-3823 fatherhood of Glasgow-3828; maternal identity and upstream ancestry are separate.

Next useful test: Check the original 1850 Lloyd row and subsequent marriage/death.

Source basis already held: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M4HM-J4K "United States, Census, 1850", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M4HM-J4K : Tue Jan 14 03:08:39 UTC 2025), Entry for Samuel Glasgo and Elizabeth Glasgo, 1850.]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.
